monthly_review.summary: This month shows increased volume and endurance focus at the cost of pace and intensity, with a notable shift toward lower HR zones and improved recovery metrics.
monthly_review.highlight: Zone 1 + Zone 2 time increased from 55% to 79% of total HR distribution — a strong aerobic base-building shift, but at the expense of Zone 3–5 stimulus that previously supported faster paces.

goal_tracker.message: You’ve already exceeded last month’s distance by 8.0 km and completed one more run — no additional running is needed this month to surpass April’s totals.

insights.title: Efficiency dip aligns with slower pacing and higher volume
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency declined from 13.66 to 13.42 m/sec per bpm, coinciding with a 19-sec/km average pace slowdown and 8.0 km increase in monthly volume — suggesting recent runs prioritized duration over metabolic economy.

insights.title: Near-total absence of high-intensity work this month
insights.body: Zone 4 dropped from 15% to 3% and Zone 5 vanished entirely (0%) — whereas last month included 4% Zone 5 efforts supporting pace development (best pace: 428 sec/km vs this month’s 447).

insights.title: Cadence improved despite slower pace and longer ground contact
insights.body: Avg cadence rose from 142 to 146 spm, yet ground contact time increased across recent runs (308–320 ms), indicating shorter, quicker steps may be compensating for reduced leg spring efficiency or fatigue.

insights.title: Consistent VO2 max and lower avg HR signal positive adaptation
insights.body: VO2 max remains stable at 37.0 mL/kg/min across all five recent runs, and average HR dropped 6 bpm month-over-month — evidence of improved cardiovascular efficiency and likely adequate recovery between sessions.

recommendations.action: Perform one 4km Zone 3 interval session: 4 x 1km @ 440–450 sec/km (7:20–7:30 min/km) with 90 sec walk/jog recovery, keeping HR between 148–156 bpm.
recommendations.reason: Reintroduces Zone 3 stimulus missing this month (only 19% vs 26% last month) and targets your current best pace (447 sec/km) to rebuild speed-endurance linkage.

recommendations.action: Add a 15-min post-run cadence drill: run easy at 155+ spm for 3 x 5 min with 1-min walk breaks, focusing on quick turnover and light footstrike (target ground contact <295 ms).
recommendations.reason: Cadence increased but stride length decreased (71–82 cm vs prior long run stride of 94 cm), suggesting neuromuscular coordination can be sharpened to improve efficiency without increasing effort.

recommendations.action: Do one 30-min Zone 2 recovery run at ≤135 bpm — no pace target, just HR discipline — following your next harder session.
recommendations.reason: Your May avg HR is 136 bpm, and 5/5 recent runs were ≥132 bpm; adding one truly low-HR session will reinforce aerobic resilience and support continued VO2 max stability.

weekly_focus.description: Re-establish neural pathways for faster turnover and intentional pace control, balancing the month’s endurance emphasis with targeted rhythm and responsiveness.
